newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Issue Dept assets rise to 3 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Issue Dept assets rise to 3 bln marks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's Issue Department boosted its assets and liabilities to three billion marks from 2.8 billion marks a week ago when the currency board system was launched, the BNB said on Monday.

The department's assets include the mark equivalent of 1.48 trillion levs in securities, 869.7 billion levs cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies, 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 11.8 billion levs in accrued intrest receivables, the BNB said in a statement.

The department's liabilities comprise 556.0 billion levs of currency in circulation, 747.8 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts, 557.8 billion levs in government deposits and accounts, 571.2 billion levs in a State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account, 17.7 billion levs in other deposits and accrued interest payable of 16.3 billion levs.

These liabilities also include a 534.7 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department that can be used for lending to sound banks, only when the functioning of the banking and payments system is threatened.
The primary objective of the Banking Department is to ensure confidence in the liquidity of the banking system and more broadly the efficient functioning of key financial markets.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund, Bulgaria introduced on Tuesday the currency board, a fixed exchange rate mechanism which requires levs in circulation to be matched by BNB foreign exchange reserves.
Under the arrangement the lev is pegged to the mark as anchor currency at 1,000 levs. The system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
The balance sheet will be published weekly. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
